title: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
abstract: arXiv:2606.15017v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Online web agents often augment a base actor with memory, workflow, or skill modules. These modules can improve performance, but they also consume test-time tokens, a cost rarely reported alongside the actor's inference cost. We study online augmentation, where this overhead is paid on every task, and re-evaluate its benefits under a fixed total inference budget. We compare AWM, ASI, and ReasoningBank with a token-matched vanilla baseline that uses the same budget for additional actor steps. Across four WebArena domains and three models, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5.4-mini, and Qwen 3.6-27B, the vanilla baseline matches or surpasses all three augmentation methods in aggregate success rate while often using fewer total tokens. We observe a similar trend on WorkArena-L1 with Qwen 3.6-27B, indicating that the effect extends to enterprise knowledge-work tasks. Our results suggest that skills and workflow memory can be useful in specific domains

translated_title: 在线技能与记忆模块总是值得其token消耗吗？面向网络智能体的预算约束研究
translated_abstract: 在线网络智能体通常通过记忆、工作流或技能模块来增强基础执行器。这些模块可以提升性能，但它们也会消耗测试时的token，而这一成本很少与执行器的推理成本一同被报告。我们研究了在线增强场景（即这种开销在每个任务上都需要支付），并在固定的总推理预算下重新评估其收益。我们将AWM、ASI和ReasoningBank与一个token匹配的原始基线进行比较，该基线将相同的预算用于额外的执行器步骤。在四个WebArena领域和三个模型（Gemini 3 Flash、GPT-5.4-mini和Qwen 3.6-27B）上，原始基线在总体成功率上匹配或超越了所有三种增强方法，同时往往使用更少的总token数。我们在WorkArena-L1上使用Qwen 3.6-27B也观察到类似趋势，表明这一效应可以延伸到企业知识工作类任务。我们的结果表明，技能和工作流记忆在特定领域中可能是有用的。
tldr: 在固定总推理预算下，token匹配的原始基线在总体成功率上匹配或超越了AWM、ASI和ReasoningBank三种技能与记忆增强方法，且往往消耗更少token，表明这些模块并非总是物有所值。
en_tdlr: Under a fixed total inference budget, a token-matched vanilla baseline matches or surpasses AWM, ASI, and ReasoningBank in aggregate success rate while often using fewer tokens, suggesting that skill and memory modules are not always worth their token cost.
